text_en: I work as an applied researcher, turning research into numbers people can use. Day to day that means advanced Excel (formulas, VBA, database-style workbooks), CSV, Power BI, Python/SQL, and both descriptive and inferential statistics. The master's research is that same habit applied to perceived trust: a web tool on Azure, the analysis in Python and Power BI, and a comparison of AI raters with students. I took Information Visualization in that program (Grade A). I use CSI/NPS when prioritizing outcomes. Master's in Technology approved September 2026 (diploma November 2026), with Grade A across all coursework. Outside work I practice memory techniques (mnemonics and memory palaces) and build AutoHotkey, Python, and other macros to speed up everyday computer work.
text_detail_en: I'm an applied researcher. A lot of what I do is taking messy operational and experiential signals and turning them into something structured enough to decide on. That usually means advanced Excel (formulas, VBA, database-style workbooks), CSV pipelines, Power BI, Python and SQL, plus descriptive and inferential statistics. The master's research is that same habit applied to perceived trust: a web tool on Azure, the analysis in Python and Power BI, and a comparison of AI raters with students. The Information Visualization coursework in that program (Grade A) shapes how I pick visuals and interaction for stakeholders. I use CSI and NPS when I need to prioritize what actually matters. I had my Master's in Technology approved in September 2026 (diploma November 2026), with Grade A across all coursework. Outside work I practice memory techniques with mnemonics and memory palaces, and I build AutoHotkey, Python, and other macros to make everyday computer work faster.
